ceiling_directive: Prove the joint influence law over the published Han–Shah sampling class, allowing its cross-cell dependence and unequal cell sizes, and propagate the resulting covariance through the spectral map.
improvement_directive: Replace the relative-survival bounded-variation and variation-rate assumptions with primitive hazard smoothness and complexity conditions for a concrete continuous-time, continuous-covariate learner, deriving the O_P(a_Kb_K) drift and influence-vector consistency directly. This would extend the unconditional result beyond the current fixed finite-stratum certificate.
critique: The limit law and bands are proved only for fixed dimensions, exact rank, exact post-transport, and independent equal-K samples in every cell; they do not establish inference under weak or selected rank or the dependent sampling structure relevant to the TCL application. The load-bearing AIPCW expansion assumes the proof-tailored condition that the total variation of Q/\widehat Q-1 is O_P(a_K), which is precisely what makes the Stieltjes remainder second order and is not implied by the cited generic L2 nuisance rates. That condition is derived only for fixed finite covariate and event-time supports with uniformly positive risk cells and clipped empirical hazards, leaving the broader censoring-robust workflow conditional on an unusually strong learner property. The Kaplan–Meier/PCR proposition proves nonzero fixed bias on a constructed relatively open exact-transport subclass, not a characterization of failure on the published class; the framing accurately leaves weak-gap inference and application validity open.
